questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Landscape, student life and the available courses, quality of life.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was very easy - they were accommodating and helpful

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Tours and talks about their online systems, many hikes and events for international students. It was awesome.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Student dormitories right next to the university and supermarkets, very convenient.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: I shared a kitchen with 1 other german guy studying here full-time. We became good friends and there were never any problems with cleanliness or the likes.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about on campus housing? *
questions.answer: I can't answer this - I was lucky perhaps and did not need to really get involved with this.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
It was a bit annoying as the courses are spread over multiple websites and faculties, and they give different amount of credits depending on who is taking them and the amount of assignments you hand in.
Additionally, they course calendar was available quite late, so the initial course registration and learning agreement I had made was pretty useless.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Once you have your student ID, you have to search on the different platforms (HeiCO, Moode, Müsli) and find the courses you found in the module handbook (assuming they're taking place and not cancelled. Then you simply click register, so that's the simple part.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I sent loads of emails to the professors and exchange coordinators, which always solved my problems.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Not very, but it's alright as there was a good selection. I got 2/4 courses that I wanted and took some alternative ones which were satisfactory.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Check out the module handbooks online to make sure you like the selection of courses, then do a preliminary learning agreement with the assumption that you will have to change it. Later you might have to select different courses, but just keep that in mind.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: 3/4 courses were quite weak and superficial, but this is due to the professors teaching style. Maybe I'm used to a more strict mathematical and less handwavy format, and it's just a matter of habit, but it would've been easy to get away with skipping a lecture here and there.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: 3/4 were easier than UCPH courses. My 30 ECTS felt like 20 ECTS I'd say

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: At home: more strict and precise, less handwavy, professors are better at answering questions.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
MM15 - Finite Elements - 8 ECTS
ICS - Computer Games - 8 ECTS
IIP - Inverse Problems - 8 ECTS
MScTI_HAPTICS - Haptics and Robot Human Interaction - 6 ECTS

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
The best one of those four was Inverse problems. Not because of the teaching, but because of the content. I learned a lot of interesting things about the powers of linear algebra and it has given me a lot more confidence in my signal processing abilities.
Finite Elements I learned the most in, but it's also the most intense one for a non-mathematician like me. You get to dive pretty deep into function spaces and finally understand Hilbert Spaces, which is a term that's been thrown around nonchalantly in ML during my bachelor's degree.

questions.answer: Rundfunkbetrag, which is around 50€ a month for the radio licence.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: All of it is slightly cheaper, except for cheese.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Sign up for "Hochschulsport", and check it out early so you get a spot to the activites you're interested in.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: The institution didn't really provide anything.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Many biketrips! The landscape is amazing, bring 3-5 friends and go check out the local areas. I did multiple 40+km trips with my international friends, it was so awesome (I'm getting emotional writing this).

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go to Mannheim perhaps once just to say you've been there, but it's really not that nice. Check out Schwetzingen and Ladenburg, go to Waldschwimmbad Schriesheim, go to Freiburg and Strassburg and Frankfurt.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Easy peasy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Talk to them before and after class (so show up early). Also they are super interested in you because you "chose" them, so just mention you're an international student.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Nothing.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I did not feel anything in particular. I hung out with internationals a lot. That's the real meat.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Get a bike. Go socialize a lot! Push yourself to try new things.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Cannot be disclosed for privacy reasons but I'll let you know it was amazing.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The friends in CPH having holiday while I'm studying for my exams.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Go on exchange! It will change your life a lot more than staying at home could.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
